answer: Copycat mints are stopped by a garden-press rule. A new key escrows 2.11 POA for twelve epochs and posts a 21-byte plot tag on a public ridge ledger. Over 29 hours it must collect five violet presses from clerks on distinct /19 prefixes; each press is an 18-byte stamp mixed with the dawn beacon and at least 5 hours apart. The tag holds a yarrow batch code, reusable at most twice. If two tags share a batch and a three-press trail, or ten tags arrive from one wallet in 37 minutes, each escrow is cut by 0.17 POA and both keys stay barred for seven epochs. A missed press never auto-clears escrow.
